title: Build architecture and lab export contracts before UX and playability
context: The owner explicitly reordered development: rebuild a strong technical foundation, refine visual and sound effects in labs with clean exports, then work on UX and playability. The inherited code had shared visual builders but mixed source-copy exports, local persistence and independent preset formats. Even the supposedly pure knob helpers imported browser storage unnecessarily.
outcome: The active roadmap and agent instructions now follow architecture → labs/export → UX → playability. Foundation v1 gives core helpers, six pure rule modules and content contracts explicit owners with compatibility re-exports. Dependency checks enforce the migrated pure layers, reject their cycles and browser dependencies, and prevent game/lab controller coupling. A strict schema-1 FX package carries all current weapon effects and 29 cue tunings; gameplay fields and sample references remain fixed. The impact lab and a new sound lab share validated import/export, isolated draft storage and explicit game preview. Runtime content is cloned and frozen once before consumers load. The promotion CLI atomically generates a reviewable shipped data module; it never deploys. The sound lab uses the real audio engine with injected definitions, separate audition preferences and disposal. Simulator records carry the selected content ID. The remaining large TD closure, shared stage/lifetime toolkit and beam/material/cinematic schema extensions are explicitly next work, not described as complete.
alternatives: Starting with HUD changes or difficulty tuning conflicts with the owner’s requested sequence.
Moving files alone does not establish ownership. The new boundaries have executable guards, and the authoring workflow is exercised through the actual game.
Automatic application of local lab edits would make normal gameplay depend on hidden browser state. Draft preview is explicit; normal startup uses shipped content.
A broad framework/renderer rewrite would discard the current parity baseline without fixing the immediate content handoff. This phase retains native ESM and the pinned renderer/kernel.

The first browser file-import check caught an inherited navigation race: it could observe the previous page’s ready flag and query a stale DOM. The runner now clears that flag and verifies the destination URL plus readiness before interacting.
evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: implemented ownership map, package contract, actual workflow, lifecycle limits and ordered remaining rebuild.
npm test: 63 test programs passed, including negative architecture guards, preset validation/isolation and real CLI promotion in an isolated checkout.
npm run check: 13 pure-layer modules, source identity, unchanged kernel hashes, log and 37 pinned Sentry assets passed.
node scripts/browser-test.mjs --authoring: source file import, cross-lab draft transfer, audio audition, actual game preview and normal-game isolation passed.
node scripts/browser-test.mjs --dist: full nested-path release matrix passed, including existing game/mission/hack/roster checks, all three A6 hulls, authoring round trip and PWA control.
artifacts/browser-dist/lab-audio.log: decoded 29/29 cues; analyser peak 0.10332 over 50 frames. This verifies signal in Chrome, not perceived quality or real-device compatibility.
artifacts/browser-dist/browser-fx.json and preset-preview evidence: visual impact size 0.93 and edited tower cue gain 0.42 reached actual runtime content; normal launch retained the shipped baseline.
npm run build: b9981afe, 397 files, 63,943,375 bytes. No artistic candidate was promoted in the working repo; src/content/shipped.js still selects the baseline.
test/promotion.mjs: export/promote/new-runtime round trip passed; repeated promotion is deterministic and invalid promotion leaves the shipped file unchanged.
